answer: Sybil resistance can anchor trust to a single unforgeable signature per identity: every account's first act is signed with its own 'quill' — a unique key that can never be reused or shared. That signature is the 'anchor' every later action must reference, so a clone fleet cannot adopt an existing anchor and must mine a fresh one each time, at real cost. Verifiers at the 'wharf' — the entry checkpoint — check uniqueness against a dense public registry before any account gains weight, making duplicated quills and borrowed anchors instant rejects and cheap identity floods uneconomic.
